subject: economics
title: Measuring Development: HDI and Beyond
welcome_lead: GDP per head misses the point - development needs broader measures.
meta_desc: A-Level Development: HDI and Sen's capabilities approach.
final_note: Development is widening choices, not just raising incomes.

concepts.def: Human Development Index - life expectancy, schooling, GNI per head.
Income measure adjusted for population size.
Sen - the freedoms people have to live the lives they value.
Multi-dimensional Poverty Index - health, education, living standards.
Maternal mortality, parliament seats, education by gender.

walkthroughs.body_html: HDI blends life expectancy, mean and expected years of schooling, and GNI per head. Scores run 0 to 1; Norway tops, Niger and Chad near the bottom.
Amartya Sen argues development is about capabilities - what people are free to do and be. Income is a means; the goal is human flourishing.
No single measure captures everything. HDI hides inequality; MPI is data hungry; capabilities resist quantification. Use multiple measures and qualitative context.
